facts.note: April 1944: The Air Ministry requisitioned the airfield and surrounding farms, roads and houses, ostensibly to accommodate military bombers.

facts.claim: 페어리 항공의 시험 비행용 비행장(Great West Aerodrome)
facts.note: Fairey Aviation needed an airfield for flight testing of aircraft designed and manufactured at its factory ... The Great West Aerodrome was used for aircraft assembly and testing.

facts.claim: 밸푸어가 책임자 · 1973년 자서전에서 공청회를 피하려 위원회를 일부러 속였다고 밝힘
facts.note: The project was headed by Harold Balfour ... wrote in his 1973 autobiography, Wings over Westminster, that he deliberately deceived the government committee into believing a requisition was necessary ... and used a wartime emergency requisition order to avoid a lengthy and costly public inquiry.

25 March 1946: Reginald Fletcher, 1st Baron Winster, the Minister of Aviation, performed the official opening ceremony. The passenger terminal was an area of Army tents and duckboarding next to the south side of the Bath Road.

facts.claim: 페어리 1930년 격납고는 20년 소송 동안 헐지 못해 소방서로 쓰임
facts.note: Fairey's 1930 hangar, in legal limbo for 20 years, and used as the Heathrow Airport fire station ... was then finally demolished.

question.hintNote: The first passenger to enter Terminal 5 ... was presented with a boarding pass by British Airways CEO Willie Walsh for the first departing flight, BA302 to Paris.
